answer.rationale: With an 18% mandated cut and no delivery buffer, switching carries onboarding risk and dual-sourcing adds cost I cannot absorb. The incumbent relationship (memory_c1) is stable and already known. The multi-year volume pricing lever (memory_c6) and the benchmarking-renegotiation playbook (memory_c4, unverified but consistent with memory_c6's cost-reduction logic) give me the best single lever to compress total cost of ownership without touching delivery logistics. Verifying memory_c2 confirms whether the low-cost alternative is genuinely viable as a credible BATNA in the negotiation; verifying memory_c6 confirms the volume-commitment pricing structure I will propose. If both records hold, I renew with the incumbent under renegotiated multi-year terms, locking a unit-cost reduction sufficient to meet the 18% target while keeping the 14-day renewal window and the 94%-utilization line undisturbed.
